description: Nancy Zimmerman – People, Process, and Fixed Income Arbitrage at Bracebridge (EP.517)

turns.en: You learn a few things during crises, you want to have liquidity, flexibility to be able to lean into dislocations, especially things where you know them well. You feel like you are positioned to take advantage of it, maybe make it go away. Every crisis teaches and reinforces that you want to stress test. You want to think carefully about what factors could cause a drawdown in your portfolio. You want to think hard about what's the difference between a drawdown and a
turns.zh: 危机之中你能学到几样东西：你希望拥有流动性、拥有灵活性，能够在市场发生错位（dislocation）的时候迎身而上，尤其是那些你非常熟悉的东西；你觉得自己处在有利位置去利用它，甚至让它消失。每一次危机都在教育并强化同一个道理：你要做压力测试，要仔细思考哪些因素可能让你的组合出现回撤，要认真想清楚回撤和……的区别

turns.en: capital impairment because those are different things. Also thinking about what doesn't work, what are you relying on in terms of institutions, courts, banks, counterparties, these kinds of things. You learn them in your first crisis and you never forget them. Stuff begins to rhyme for you. The most important thing that we learn is good people who are curious and have thought through things and can maintain their curiosity, their bearings, and have a real sense of rigor
turns.zh: ……资本受损（capital impairment）的区别，因为这是两回事。还要思考哪些环节会失灵：你在机构、法院、银行、交易对手这些事情上依赖的到底是什么。你在第一次危机里学会这些，就永远不会忘记。一切开始在你眼前像押韵一样重演。我们学到的最重要的一点是：好的、有好奇心、把问题想透、能够保持好奇与定力的人……

turns.en: and purpose are vital to those moments. I'm Ted Sides and this is Capital Allocators. My guest on today's show is Nancy Zimmerman, the co-founder and managing partner of Bracebridge Capital, a $13 billion alternative asset manager specializing in fixed income arbitrage that she founded over 30 years ago in 1994 alongside Gabe Sunshine with Capital from David Swenson at Yale.
turns.zh: ……并且真正具有严谨精神和目标感的人，对那些时刻至关重要。我是 Ted Seides，这里是 Capital Allocators。今天节目的嘉宾是 Nancy Zimmerman，Bracebridge Capital 的联合创始人兼管理合伙人——这是一家规模 130 亿美元、专注固定收益套利（fixed income arbitrage）的另类资产管理公司，三十多年前的 1994 年，她与 Gabe Sunshine 一起创立了它，资本来自耶鲁大学的 David Swenson。

turns.en: Our conversation traces Nancy's evolution from pricing securities to investing and the enduring sources of inefficiency in fixed income markets. We discussed the nature of arbitrage opportunities and their persistence over time and then turned to hunting for mispricings today across developed market rates, structured credit, corporates, and emerging markets.
turns.zh: 我们的对话将追溯 Nancy 从给证券定价到做投资的演变之路，以及固定收益市场中长期存在的无效率的根源。我们讨论了套利机会的本质、它们为何能穿越时间持续存在，然后转向今天在发达市场利率、结构化信用、公司债和新兴市场里搜寻错误定价。

turns.en: Along the way, we cover Bracebridge's process for sourcing ideas, assessing relative value, determining position sizes, constructing a portfolio, and managing risk. We close with building a team, aligning the organization and its clients, investing in today's exciting and unusual environment, and transferring investment knowledge to work on the investment committee and brand science research at Nancy's alma mater Brown University. Nancy is among the
turns.zh: 期间我们会谈到 Bracebridge 寻找想法（sourcing ideas）、评估相对价值、决定头寸规模、构建组合和管理风险的流程。最后我们谈到团队建设、让组织与客户利益保持一致、在今天这个既令人兴奋又不寻常的环境里投资，以及把投资知识迁移到 Nancy 的母校布朗大学的投资委员会和脑科学（brain science）研究工作中。Nancy 是……

turns.en: Why don't you take me all the way back to the influences growing up that had some impact on what's happened today? I grew up outside Chicago in Skokie, Illinois, and I went to Brown. I was sophomore at Brown where I was doing some math and some computer science, making some large metal sculptures. For Christmas, I got a job at a art gallery. Sometime before I got home to take that job, it went out of business. I came from a family where you had a job. I needed to get a
turns.zh: 何不带我一路回到那些影响了今天种种事情的成长经历？我在芝加哥郊外的伊利诺伊州 Skokie 长大，然后上了布朗大学。我在布朗读大二的时候，学一些数学和计算机科学，还做一些大型金属雕塑。圣诞节时我得到一份美术馆的工作，结果还没等我回家去上班，它就倒闭了。我家里观念是人人都得有一份工作，所以我需要找一份……

turns.en: summer job. My sister, who honestly is perpetually had my back my whole life, introduced me to some guys who had about five years earlier dropped out of MIT to start an auctions arbitrage firm at the Chicago Board of Options Exchange at the Sebo backed by some grain traders, O'Connor and Associates. They gave me a summer job running messages, doing things, super eye-opening. I found out about options markets. It was a combination of news and math
turns.zh: ……暑期工。我姐姐——说实话她这辈子一直在给我撑腰——把我介绍给了几个人，他们大约五年前从 MIT 辍学，在芝加哥期权交易所创办了一家套利公司，背后是一些做谷物的交易商，就是 O'Connor and Associates。他们给了我一份暑期工作，跑腿传话、打杂，特别开眼界。我由此认识了期权市场。它是新闻和数学……

turns.en: puzzles. I was lucky with my timings. In 1983, he says, just learning how to use a personal computer. He put somebody on the floor of an exchange with a shark. It has quotes. You can figure out how to manipulate them in a tiny little program so that you can arbitrage the difference between that Kansas City value line and the S&P 100. The way that they used to do this before this moment is they would make a piece of paper. They would write down every price they
turns.zh: ……谜题的结合体。我时机踩得很准。1983 年，正是大家刚学会怎么用个人电脑的时候，他们派一个人坐到交易所场内，带着报价。你能琢磨出怎么用一个极小的程序去处理这些报价，从而在堪萨斯城的报价线和 S&P 100 之间做套利。在那个年代之前他们是怎么做的呢？做一张纸，把能想到的其中一个标的的所有价格都写下来……

turns.en: could imagine for one of them and then where they wanted to do the arbitrage on the other. This is replaced by five lines of code that had huge pedagogical interest in educating everyone because they sat in crowds or people always giving away money. They went through a lot of trouble to make sure that everybody who worked there understood how to price things, put call parity, where the arbitrage free forward was. They were careful to go through in a very detailed way.
turns.zh: ……再写另一个标的上他们想做套利的位置。这件事被五行代码取代了。他们有着巨大的教学热忱，要把每个人都教明白，因为他们坐在人群中央，看着别人一直在白送钱。他们费了很大的功夫，确保在那儿工作的每个人都理解怎么给东西定价、什么是看跌看涨平价（put-call parity）、无套利远期在哪里。他们非常细致地走一遍……

turns.en: What we know and is like physics, what is an assumption so we can make the Black Shoals work. They would do these things that were time intense. You would have somebody who was the partner in charge of risk arbitrage go through how to do a binomial tree to figure out how the math worked a very big focus on the distribution of returns of a trade, what it meant to make prices, how one price related to another, thinking about when we use models to describe prices
turns.zh: ……我们知道的东西，那些有点像物理学的东西，以及哪些是假设、好让 Black-Scholes 能成立。他们会做这些很耗时的事情：负责风险套利的那位合伙人会带你走一遍二叉树（binomial tree），弄明白数学是怎么转的。他们极其关注一笔交易的回报分布、报价意味着什么、一个价格和另一个价格如何关联，思考我们什么时候用模型去描述价格和……

turns.en: volatility, what goes into that, what were our assumptions. They spent a lot of times making sure that you understood how to price a box, calling a put of one strike versus a call in a put of another. They did a little bit gloss over of why markets move. They were uninterested in macro or any things that weren't bottoms up around pricing options or pricing other derivatives that drew your attention to this part of the program. I spent a lot of time at Brown after
turns.zh: ……波动率，模型里放了什么，我们的假设是什么。他们花了很多时间确保你理解怎么给一个 box 组合定价：某一个行权价的 put，对比另一个行权价的 call 加 put。至于市场为什么会波动，他们有点一笔带过。他们对宏观、对一切不是自下而上给期权或其他衍生品定价的东西不感兴趣——也正是这一点把你吸引到项目的这一部分。在那之后我在布朗花了大量时间……

turns.en: that doing coursework halfway through Brown. You can decide I want to know everything there is to know about statistics and probability. It is interesting to see how small things that are serendipitous feed into what happens. Then I went back to O'Connor after I said, if you get back here on June 5th and take this test, you can go to the floor and make prices in Swiss franc options, which was the third market for Swiss franc options, which means there's six people sitting at the merc
turns.zh: ……修课。在布朗读到一半，你可以下定决心：我要把统计学和概率论里该知道的全都知道。有趣的是，那些偶然的小事会怎样汇入后来发生的一切。然后我回了 O'Connor——他们说，只要你 6 月 5 日回来并通过一场考试，你就可以去场内报瑞士法郎期权的价格。那是瑞郎期权的第三市场，意味着有六个人坐在 MERC……

turns.en: who are looking at boards to see if they can arbitrage or make prices that are wide enough to capture some more bid offer and lay the risk off in the other two markets. It was a great experience. I learned to make prices. I was on the floor doing the middle of Plaza Accord when they decided we're just going to put the dollar in a different place. Those things stick with you to see big currency interventions, to understand how all the pieces work together,
turns.zh: ……盯着行情板，看自己能不能套利，或者报出足够宽的价格多赚点买卖价差，再把风险在另外两个市场平掉。那是一段非常棒的经历。我学会了报价。我在场内经历了广场协议（Plaza Accord）的中段——他们决定要把美元放到一个不一样的位置上。这样的事会刻在你身上：亲眼看到大规模的货币干预，理解所有零件怎么协同运作，……

turns.en: how currencies and bonds work together. I was a market maker in currency option, probably all the majors. O'Connor did a tie up with some guys for Chicago, which was a big deal internally.
turns.zh: ……货币和债券怎么相互作用。我做过外汇期权的做市商，大概所有主要货币都做过。O'Connor 和芝加哥的一批人达成了一个合作，这在公司内部是件大事。

turns.en: At some point, they started a bond initiative. The bond options at the board of trade was a huge crowd. The futures were active. It was a lucrative business for them, and they decided they should be more involved in the O'Connor business. They hired some people. I went over that. I don't really remember why. I found out about bonds. I found out there's all these cash flows. At that time, there were only three instruments describing U.S. risk-free interest rates. Now, there's 48 in the
turns.zh: 后来某个时候，他们启动了债券这条线。交易所的债券期权是个极其拥挤的交易，期货也很活跃。对他们来说是门赚钱的生意，于是他们决定自己应该更深入地参与 O'Connor 的业务。他们招了一些人，我转了过去。我已经不太记得为什么了。我认识了债券，发现原来有这么多现金流。那时候，描述美国无风险利率的工具只有三个，现在有 48 个分布在……

turns.en: first three years of the curve. I found out about bonds, basis trade, cheapest to deliver plays, cash your future arbitrage, doing market making.
turns.zh: ……曲线的前三年里。我认识了债券、基差交易（basis trade）、最便宜可交割券（cheapest to deliver）的玩法、现券-期货套利（cash-futures arbitrage）、做市。

turns.en: How did you get from that initial seat to eventually starting Bracebridge? There was a crash in 87. This one stocks used to go down. O'Connor was in an equity place, a little bit of a retrenchment into that. I went to Goldman to try to see if I couldn't help them build a platform that made prices in U.S. treasury options everywhere. It was exciting. I learned a lot of things. I spent a third of my time
turns.zh: 从最初那个席位，你是怎么一步步走到最后创办 Bracebridge 的？87 年发生了股灾。原来股票是可以大跌的。O'Connor 在股票业务上有敞口，在那上面做了一点收缩。我去了高盛，想看看能不能帮他们搭一个平台，到处给美国国债期权报价。那很令人兴奋，我学到很多。我把三分之一的时间花在……

turns.en: making prices or managing somebody who made prices, a third of my time doing the kind of things you do to have a vibrant, fabulous business like Goldman has, building models, cultivating clients, working with clients, educating salespeople. I spent a third of my time proprietary trading, trying to take advantage of the difference between two completely fungible cash flows in the U.S. Treasury curve or two options that were on the same part of the
turns.zh: ……报价或者管理一个报价的人上；三分之一的时间做那种支撑高盛这样旺盛精彩生意所需的事情——建模型、拓展客户、和客户共事、培训销售人员；三分之一的时间做自营交易，试着去利用美国国债曲线上两笔完全可互换的现金流之间的差异，或者收益率曲线同一段上的两个期权……

turns.en: yield curve, stripping and reconstituting bonds. That third was where it lit me up. I was always interested in figuring out why is this happening, how much worse is it going to get, what's going on here, what are the flows that make this happen, what are the institutional arrangements that make it happen. I wanted to have my whole day be like that last third of the day. I went out into the world to try to find a way to do that. Eventually, a lot of wanderings leave me in an office sitting
turns.zh: ……之间的差异，把债券拆开（stripping）再复原（reconstituting）。那三分之一才是让我眼睛发亮的地方。我一直想知道：这件事为什么会发生、还会糟糕到什么程度、这里到底在发生什么、是什么资金流让它发生、是什么制度安排让它发生。我想让我一整天都像那最后的三分之一。于是我走进外面的世界，想办法做到这一点。兜兜转转，最终我坐在一间办公室里，和……

turns.en: with David Twenson and Dean Takahashi, David was the grandfather of the SWAL, talking about how he built that and LIBOR and why aren't these things efficient. I tell David what I do, there's a lot of alpha in fixed income. There's too many instruments describing the exact same things.
turns.zh: ……David Swenson 和 Dean Takahashi 在一起——David 是捐赠基金投资这门事业的祖师爷——聊他是怎么打造它的，聊 LIBOR，聊为什么这些东西会没有效率。我告诉 David 我做的事：固定收益里有很多 alpha，描述同一个东西的工具实在太多了。

turns.en: You can generate an uncorrelated return by putting them together and make a diversifying set of cash flows. He loves the idea. I said, isn't somebody else doing this? He said, no, every time I meet somebody who says they're doing this, they spend a lot of their risk capital and time guessing which way rates are going. We immediately click because we both have this bedrock idea that this is not a good sport to play at the same time as trying to do what we then
turns.zh: 你把它们组合起来，做一个分散化的现金流集合，就能生成一条不相关的回报。他很喜欢这个点子。我说，难道没有别人在做这个吗？他说，没有。每当我遇到一个自称做这件事的人，他们都把大量风险资本和时间花在猜利率往哪个方向走上。我们立刻一拍即合，因为我们都有一个基石般的信念：一边去做我们后来称之为固定收益套利的事、一边去赌利率方向，……

turns.en: called fixed income arbitrage. It was a start of a beautiful partnership. I had this unbelievable privilege of building a tool that I hope helped the endowment diversify without giving up expected returns. They helped Gabe Sunshine when I become investors, taught us the difference between pricing something and investing in something. On that day when I was sitting there, we weren't investors. We knew how to price things, but I hadn't been an investor. What do you mean by
turns.zh: ……这不是个好的玩法。那是一段美好伙伴关系的开端。我有种难以置信的幸运，能够去打造一个我希望能帮助捐赠基金在不放弃预期回报的情况下做分散的工具。当我开始成为投资人的时候，他们——还有 Gabe Sunshine——教会了我们给一个东西定价和对它投资的区别。当年坐在那里的时候，我们还不是投资人。我们会给东西定价，但我还没有当过投资人。你说的……是什么意思？

turns.en: the difference between pricing something and investing in something? How do we decide between the duration of opportunities? How do we think about how things inside the portfolio co-vary?
turns.zh: ……给一个东西定价和对它投资的区别是什么？我们怎么在机会的久期（duration）之间做取舍？我们怎么思考组合内部各项如何一起共变？

turns.en: To think hard about catalysts and holding periods. To think about the difference between capital impairment and a drawdown. All these super important things. It was a special professional opportunity. Yale became a seed investor. We rented a little office here in Boston. How long do you think it took you to go from a small team of two who knew how to price things to understanding the trade-offs that went into building a portfolio?
turns.zh: 要深入思考催化剂和持有期，思考资本受损和回撤的区别——所有这些超级重要的事情。那是一段特别的职业机遇。耶鲁成了种子投资人，我们在波士顿这里租了一间小办公室。你觉得，从一个只有两个人、懂定价的小团队，到理解构建一个组合所需的各种权衡，要花多长时间？

turns.en: One of the things about this business is that there's a new puzzle every day and you're learning things that's rich and deep. It is probably not until sometime in 98 or 99 that we are fully baked investors thinking about things in the way that we would think about them now in terms of how to allocate a dollar of arbitrage capital across the opportunity set that we feel comfortable.
turns.zh: 这个生意的一个特点是，每天都有新谜题，而你要学的东西既丰富又深。大概要到 98 或 99 年的某个时候，我们才算是完全成型的投资人——会用我们今天的方式去思考：怎么把一美元的套利资本，分配在我们心里有底的机会集上。

turns.en: We know everything about in-fix-income arbitrage and have a process that is detailed and allows us to compare this to that. Would I rather do something that was a longer duration for a bigger edge? Is it arbitrage? How long will it take? Is there a catalyst? How do we know this?
turns.zh: 我们把固定收益套利里该知道的都知道了，也有一个足够细致的流程，能让我们把这个和那个拿来比较。我是宁愿做一个久期更长、但优势更大的机会吗？这是套利吗？要花多长时间？有催化剂吗？我们凭什么知道？

turns.en: How did it get here? What will make it converge again? It's probably some place in that time. Somehow that was still a quarter century ago. That was a quarter century ago.
turns.zh: 价格怎么会走到这里？什么会让它重新收敛？大概就是那个时间段里的某个时点。一晃眼，那都已经是四分之一个世纪以前的事了。四分之一世纪以前了。

turns.en: As we sit here today, how do you describe the value proposition of Bracebridge as a firm? I think about the investment strategy that we're delivering to people, how it can help them meet their goals when they're building a portfolio. Our strategy is an alpha generating strategy that should allow you to diversify without giving up expected return. It should be completely uncorrelated to the general level of rates, the shape of the yield curve, equity levels,
turns.zh: 站在今天，你怎么描述 Bracebridge 这家公司的价值主张？我会去想我们交付给大家的投资策略，想它在人们构建组合时怎么帮助他们达成目标。我们的策略是一个生成 alpha 的策略，应该让你在不放弃预期回报的前提下做分散。它应该和利率的总体水平、收益率曲线的形状、股票的水平……

turns.en: or to any currency. You can think about your asset liability management, what are my real assets, my liabilities, and this thing where you add a diversification instrument that's uncorrelated, especially to the downside, changes the profile and what your return is. You'll see that you add in 20 or 30% absolute return that is legitimately absolute return. You get superior total returns because you get more compounding. This diminution involved is relevant for delivering good risk
turns.zh: ……以及任何货币都完全不相关。你可以去想你的资产负债管理：我的真实资产是什么、我的负债是什么？当你加进一个不相关的分散化工具，尤其是在下行时不相关，你的风险回报面貌和你拿到的回报就变了。你会发现你加进了 20% 或 30% 的绝对回报，而且名正言顺是绝对回报。你会获得更好的总回报，因为你得到了更多复利。这里涉及的波动消减，对交付好的风险调整……

turns.en: adjusted returns. We're focused not on the firm that's Bracebridge, but on what we're delivering in terms of an investment vehicle. I'd love to tease through how you do it. It started as a firm of two people as much different today. How do you view the inputs of what it takes to deliver some uncorrelated alpha generating return stream? We're looking for inefficiencies across two things that are similar, substantially similar, or can be made to be similar through accounts.
turns.zh: ……后回报是有意义的。我们关注的不是 Bracebridge 这家公司本身，而是我们作为投资载体在交付什么。我很想请你梳理一下你们是怎么做到的。它起步时是一家只有两个人的公司，和今天已经很不一样了。你怎么看交付一条不相关、能生成 alpha 的回报流所需要的投入要素？我们寻找的是两个相似、大体相似、或者可以通过账务安排变得相似的东西之间的无效率。

turns.en: Bonds are a great place to do this because they mature or they default. We try to have people become extremely expert in markets so that they can have the technical rigor from a bottom up to understand how to price every instrument, how it's contractually constructed, how it trades, what kind of institutional vagaries there are around it. We have people in markets who are expert in those markets that are coming out with this different view, trying to understand
turns.zh: 债券是做这件事的好地方，因为债券要么到期、要么违约。我们努力让人对市场变得极其专业，让他们有自下而上的技术严谨性，去理解每个工具怎么定价、合约怎么构造、怎么交易、围绕它有哪些制度上的怪癖。我们在各个市场都有深耕该市场的人，带着各自不同的视角，试图理解……

turns.en: how to price things correctly. What should you pay for this? We have people in structured products. We have corporates. We have an emerging market group. Then we have our oldest business, a developed markets group, which is more people than we had then, more computers, more technology, doing a lot of the same things because there are still inefficiencies in developed market rates, which is incredible. What was the evolution of Bracebridge from where you
turns.zh: ……怎么正确定价，一样东西该付多少钱。我们有人做结构化产品，有人做公司债，有一个新兴市场组。然后是我们最老的业务——发达市场组，里面的人比我们当年整个公司还多，电脑更多，技术更多，做的还是很多同样的事，因为发达市场利率里居然还有无效率，简直不可思议。Bracebridge 从起步的地方是怎么演变到……

turns.en: started to these four areas of corporate, structured credit, emerging markets, and DM rates? Those are four stories that are all different. Structured product, natural outgrowth of being mortgage geeks. It gives sometimes a huge mortgage, trade CMOs at Goldman, trained by a guy who can price an IOPO in Lotus 123, wind up trading the whole compendium of things that are around resume mortgage and commercial mortgage as soon as people try and put other collateral and vats
turns.zh: ……公司债、结构化信用、新兴市场和发达市场利率这四个领域的？那是四个完全不同的故事。结构化产品是我们作为抵押贷款极客的自然延伸：从有时规模巨大的抵押贷款交易，到高盛交易 CMO，师从一个能用 Lotus 1-2-3 给 IO/PO 定价的人，最后到只要人们想把别的抵押品放进结构化产品里，我们几乎交易所有围绕住宅抵押和商业抵押的东西。

turns.en: that make structured product. Corporates, a little bit different path. It begins in the early 2000s when we have tranched corporate risk, take the hundred name index, slice them up, first default, second default, third default. At that time, we trade options on them. I don't really know why it was completely necessary, but we can help ourselves. It's not just us, the home market trades options on them. All that stuff has to be priced in a way that's
turns.zh: 公司债走的是不太一样的路。它始于 2000 年代初，当时有分层切块的公司债风险：把一百只成分组成的指数切开——第一次违约、第二次违约、第三次违约。那时候我们还交易它们上面的期权。我不知道那有什么完全必要的理由，但我们忍不住。不只是我们，市场上也有人在交易它们。所有这些东西的定价必须以自洽的方式……

turns.en: coherent. The hundred names have to go together. That gives way to single name CDS. Once they're single name CDS, we have a bond. We have CDS into which it's deliverable. There has to be an arbitrage relationship to those things. That is out of whack during various times. As we roll through the financial crisis, it gets completely insane. We have a lot of basis packages that leaves us with a way to immunize corporate credit risk at a single name level. We can begin to price out a
turns.zh: ……做得连贯。一百个名字必须对得上。然后演进到单一标的 CDS（credit default swap，信用违约互换）。有了单一标的 CDS，我们有债券，有可交付该债券的 CDS，这两者之间必然存在套利关系，而它在各个时期都会走样。当我们穿越金融危机时，它完全疯狂了。我们做了大量基差组合，由此得到一种在单一标的层面免疫公司信用风险的方法。我们可以开始把一个……

turns.en: capital stack. The probability that this company either defaults or pays has to be the same for every place in the capital stack. What happened after the GFC? We wind up with this pretty interesting business sometime around the GFC. Spring shoots come up, people start re-levering. During that period where people are starting to re-lever, things come down. Interest rates are low. Central banks are keeping things low. There's many bonds issued. They're in different currencies. People
turns.zh: ……资本结构层次（capital stack）逐层定价出来。这家公司违约或偿付的概率，在资本结构的每个位置都必须相同。金融危机之后发生了什么？我们在金融危机前后做成了一个相当有意思的业务。春笋般冒出来——人们开始重新加杠杆。在大家开始重新加杠杆的那段时期，利率往下走，央行把一切压在低位，很多债券发出来，以不同货币计价。有些连……

turns.en: who don't even have a corporate presence are issuing countries in their currency. All this stuff leaves to a lot of inefficiencies and corporates. Now we can hedge them in IG or in risky credit. It becomes obvious to us that this is a place to do the same thing that we do the rest of the platform. EM is the gift that keeps giving. There is a general dislike. You don't want to have such a big position. A lot of people want just a little EM. There's an index. It's
turns.zh: ……公司实体都不存在的发行人，发行国用自己的货币发债。这一切在公司债里留下了大量无效率。现在我们可以在投资级（IG）或风险信用里对冲它们。对我们来说很明显，这里是把我们在平台其他部分做的那套照搬过来的地方。新兴市场是那个不断给予的礼物。市场有一种普遍的嫌弃：你不想要太大的头寸，很多人只想要一点点 EM。有一个指数，它是一个……

turns.en: an emerging market benchmark index. There's dollar bonds in the index. If there's things that are outside the index, they're inefficient. We can have a pair of a US dollar bond and another currency, same Able Gore, often defaulted, often cross-defaulted under competent jurisdiction. When you swap all the cash flows back to a single currency, they'll have different discount rates. People issue bonds
turns.zh: ……新兴市场基准指数。指数里有美元债。如果指数之外有东西，那些东西就是无效率的。我们可以做一对组合：一笔美元债和一笔另一种货币的债，同一个债务人，常常违约过，常常在不同司法管辖区下交叉违约。当你把所有现金流换汇回同一种货币时，它们会有不同的贴现率。人们发的债券……

turns.en: with calls, with puts, with resets. All this stuff's got to get priced. It's not a place where people naturally think they can get involved without deciding they care about the credit of the country.
turns.zh: ……带 call 的、带 put 的、带利率重置的。这些全都得有人定价。那里不是一个你觉得不用先决定自己在不在乎一个国家的信用、就能随便参与的地方。

turns.en: It's been a reliable place to find alpha. Then we have our oldest business, which is rates, which is fabulous. If you told me in 1994 that I would still be finding opportunities and develop market rates today, I would have thought you were nuts. We thought, well, base this trade until we can't base this trade. Here we are. I would have expected things to become more efficient over time, but instead we have better tools, a better team with more experience, more diversity of perspectives,
turns.zh: 它一直是一个可靠地找到 alpha 的地方。然后是我们最老的业务——利率，太妙了。如果你在 1994 年告诉我，我今天还会在发达市场利率里找到机会，我会觉得你疯了。我们当时的想法是：做基差交易，一直做到做不了为止。结果我们就这么走到了今天。我本来以为时间会让一切更有效率，结果我们却有了更好的工具、更强的团队、更多的经验、更多元的视角……

turns.en: better path to this moment. We can aggregate a lot of information across the portfolio. We can do risk management in a more fluid way. Markets are bigger and more complex.
turns.zh: ……更好的通往今天的路径。我们能在整个组合中聚合大量信息，能以更灵活的方式做风险管理。市场更大了，也更复杂了。

turns.en: How do you think about the potential for another adjacency coming into your core four markets? At this point, the waterfront's wide enough that most of the time when we see something, it's in the seams. People will develop instruments to help everybody manage their own financial situation. Usually, if you make something special for an investor or set of investors, if they don't want it anymore, doesn't trade that well after they have to get rid of it.
turns.zh: 你怎么看下一个相邻业务进入你们核心四大市场的可能性？到了今天，我们的水域已经足够宽，大多数时候我们看到的机会都在缝隙里。人们会发明各种工具来帮大家管理自己的财务状况。通常来说，如果你为某个或某类投资者量身定做一样东西，一旦他们不想要了，他们被迫出手之后的交易表现就不怎么样。

turns.en: Over the course of time, when you find one of these inefficiencies, why don't the markets price them away? Why do they persist over decades?
turns.zh: 随着时间推移，当你找到这些无效率之一时，为什么市场没有把它们定价掉？为什么它们能持续几十年？

turns.en: A lot of inefficiencies come from places where you have a constrained economic agent. You have investor habitat. You have market segmentation. You have somebody narrowing a mandate as a way to govern a manager. People create these indexes to meter performance. They quickly become strategies themselves. You have the ratings agencies that go into creating the index itself.
turns.zh: 很多无效率来自存在受约束的经济主体。你有投资者栖息地（investor habitat），有市场分割，有人把投资授权（mandate）越收越窄来治理管理人。人们造出这些指数来衡量业绩，它们很快自己就变成了策略。还有评级机构，它们参与了指数本身的构建。

turns.en: Ratings are positively serially correlated. We know they're backward looking. That creates some inefficiency. We do see benchmark driven passive investing, this proliferation of exchange traded funds, which have to create and destroy things in a very mechanical way.
turns.zh: 评级是正序列相关的，我们知道它们是向后看的，这就制造了一些无效率。我们也看到基准驱动的被动投资，看到交易所交易基金（ETF）的大量增殖，它们必须以极其机械的方式创建和销毁头寸。

turns.en: If you add a little leverage to that, some very unusual things go on. We have some second order things that can happen. We see herding and crowding and all the things we've seen since Kindleburger. Whenever there's newness, new instruments, a change in the level of rates or volatility, market ownership, shifting ownership, a set of solvent guys deciding they just want to have a different amount of borrowing. Those things create opportunities.
turns.zh: 再在上面加一点杠杆，就会发生一些很不寻常的事，会出现一些二阶效应。我们看到羊群和拥挤，看到自 Kindleberger 以来我们看到的一切。只要有新的东西——新的工具、利率水平或波动率的变化、市场所有权的转移、一批有偿付能力的人决定想要不同规模的借贷——这些都会创造机会。

turns.en: As you look at the fullness of time of doing this, what are some of the significant changes in being able to find the opportunities today than when you started? We find opportunities a lot of different ways. All the old ways we used to find opportunities, which did involve computers and data feeds then, and still do now even more. How do you find two things that are basically the same thing and they have different prices? The way that we found is by having curious people who are expert
turns.zh: 回看你们做这一行的整个过程，和你刚开始的时候相比，今天找到机会这件事有哪些重大变化？我们用很多不同的方式找机会。我们过去找机会的所有老办法——当年就涉及电脑和数据流，现在更是如此。你怎么找到两个本质相同、价格却不同的东西？我们发现的办法，是靠那些好奇的、专业的、……

turns.en: in a market embedded and looking at everything and trying to price everything that's going on. Sometimes you find things using all those things together. Here's an example that just pops into my mind. There was a REIT that was running out of cash or they had some debt covenants. They couldn't pay any more interest, but they could still borrow money. We found them using modern techniques. It's a REIT. It's a focus on health care in real estate. They didn't have a planned
turns.zh: ……在市场里深耕的人，看所有东西，试着给正在发生的一切定价。有时候把所有这些合在一起就能找到东西。这儿有个我刚想到的例子。有一家 REIT（房地产投资信托）现金快用完了，或者说它有债务条款的限制：不能再付利息了，但还能借钱。我们用现代技术手段找到了它。它是一家 REIT，专注于医疗保健地产。它没有计划中的……

turns.en: refinance revolver. They had this rule that they couldn't pay any more interest. They were allowed to borrow money. They had unencumbered property. We ring fenced some property, lent them the money against the property. With full disclosure, everyone knowing we're able to hedge out whether or not this REIT survived or not by shorting another part of the capital structure. This is a joint venture between our structure products team and our corporates team. It worked out until like you're
turns.zh: ……再融资循环贷款。它有条规则：不能再付利息，但允许借钱。它有未设押的物业。我们圈出（ring-fence）一部分物业，以这些物业作抵押把钱借给它，完全透明披露，所有人都知道我们可以通过做空资本结构的另一部分，来对冲这家 REIT 到底能不能活下来。这是我们结构化产品团队和公司债团队的联合项目。这笔交易做得很漂亮，相当于你……

turns.en: borrowing at eight and a half. You're lending to the same name at 11 and a quarter and you're actually secured on your long side. This one was found using some combination of industrious person with a lot of data and a way to sort through it. Some actual outgoing phone calls and sourcing of the thing, structuring with lawyers, people who figure out how to ring fence the collateral that you want to encumber. When you surface up something that looks like an
turns.zh: ……以 8.5 借钱，以 11.25 贷给同一个主体，而且多头那边实际上有抵押保障。这一笔是靠勤快的人、大量数据和一套筛选方法组合找出来的：真的打电话出去找资产，跟律师一起做结构设计，有人去琢磨怎么把你想要设押的抵押品隔离出来。当你从一堆看起来像机会的东西中——在一个充满各种机会的宇宙里——捞出一个机会时，……

turns.en: opportunity in a universe of lots of different opportunities, what goes into the research and the assessment to determine whether it's a good fit for you to put into a portfolio?
turns.zh: ……什么样的研究和评估能决定它是不是适合放进你的组合？

turns.en: First, we try to think about what is the opportunity? Is it arbitrage? Why is this happening? Is there catalyst? How will we get out of this? Will it be the maturity or will they default? How much capital could we use up on our pair? Do we know that from using a model? Do we know that from some first principles because maybe one side's completely unlevered or something like that?
turns.zh: 首先，我们试着去想：这个机会是什么？是套利吗？为什么会这样？有催化剂吗？我们怎么退出？是等到期，还是它会违约？我们这对交易可能用掉多少资本？这是模型告诉我们的，还是我们从第一性原理就知道？因为也许某一侧完全没加杠杆，或者诸如此类？

turns.en: How does it compare to what we're getting paid for doing substantially the same thing in another area that can be in another name in the same market or it can be across the platform in a different part of the portfolio? Would like to make sure that we're getting the highest risk-adjusted returns for doing arbitrage? We think that is a place where we can craft a portfolio that has good risk-adjusted returns and also take responsibility for doing that
turns.zh: 和我们在别的领域做实质相同的事情所拿到的报酬相比如何？那可能是同一市场里的另一个名字，也可能是跨平台、组合里的另一块。我们想确保做套利拿到的是最高的风险调整后回报。我们认为，在这样的地方我们既能打造一个有良好风险调整后回报的组合，也能为此负责——……

turns.en: through alignment with our investors. When you go from the individual trade to creating a portfolio, how do you build the portfolio? Fundamentally, the first thing we do is look at things on a bottom-up basis. What is the opportunity? Then we try to look at how are these things correlated with each other? Do they come from the same force that's creating the inefficiency? Are they in the same sector? Is there some communal force that's making them
turns.zh: ……通过与投资人利益一致来实现。当你从单笔交易进到构建组合，你们怎么搭这个组合？根本上，我们做的第一件事是自下而上地看：这个机会是什么？然后我们看这些东西之间如何相关。它们来自同一个制造无效率的力量吗？它们在同一个板块吗？有没有某种共同力量让它们……

turns.en: correlated and then could there be in some other world? We build a portfolio on a completely forward-looking basis trying to get opportunities that we see to take advantage of inefficiencies, to compete against each other, to have what we hope is the best risk-adjusted return across the portfolio on a forward-looking basis. We do a bunch of stress testing to try to make sure that we have been careful about how things will be correlated, especially in the downside case.
turns.zh: ……相关？然后在别的世界里会不会不同？我们完全以面向未来的方式构建组合，让我们看到的机会去利用无效率、彼此竞争，希望在前瞻的基础上让全组合的风险调整后回报最好。我们做大量压力测试，努力确保我们对事物将如何相关是谨慎的，尤其是在下行情景里。

turns.en: You want to have some diversification across the thing because you want to make sure that you have buying power to do things on a crazy day when people are selling things. They don't want to be selling them at the price, but they don't have much of a choice. That's an elemental part of it.
turns.zh: 你要在组合里保持一定的分散化，因为你要确保在疯狂的日子——当人们在卖东西的时候——你有购买力去做事。他们并不想按那个价格卖，但他们没太多选择。这是这个生意最根本的部分之一。

turns.zh: ……经济。投资塑造明天的企业。到 brookfield.com/own 了解你如何拥有下一个时代。这不是出售要约，也不是投资建议。投资有风险，包括损失资本。好，回到节目。你们怎么思考头寸规模？我们思考头寸规模时，必须去想这个东西和其他东西在总量上如何相关，而不是把它当成孤零零的一个头寸。你要……

turns.zh: ……有一些集中度方面的准则：你的资产负债表上，某一类市场或某一个名字上最多放多少。有些套利的产生，恰恰是因为人们认定这个是坏的、那个是好的，而它们其实完全是一回事。你还是要去想，你资产负债表上那一款“风味”的东西总共有多少，因为人们可能突然就不喜欢那一类了。

turns.en: You have to think really hard about if you're doing things that are secured, you have a security interest in something that collateral is going to co-vary with the sector that it's in. You need to think about that as well. Those things wind up constraining what you think is sensible to do. Position sizing is going to fall out from a bottom's up process. You're going to have some overarching ideas about concentration. This is
turns.zh: 如果你做的是有担保的东西，你必须认真想：你对某个东西拥有担保权益（security interest），而那个抵押品会和它所处的板块一起共变，这也要考虑。这些因素最终会约束你认为什么才是合理的做法。头寸规模会从自下而上的流程里自然得出。你会有一些关于集中度的总体性想法。这是……

turns.en: something you do get with 34 years. You build up the portfolio based on your best expectations. Every now and then, something goes awry. LTCM back in the day, 2008, COVID. What did you learn during those crisis periods? You learn a few things during crises. You want to have liquidity, flexibility to be able to lean into dislocations, especially things where you know them well.
turns.zh: ……你做了 34 年才会有的东西。你基于自己最好的预期搭起组合，然后时不时地，有些事情会出岔子。当年的 LTCM、2008 年、新冠疫情。你在那些危机时期学到了什么？危机之中你能学到几样东西：你希望拥有流动性、拥有灵活性，能够在市场发生错位的时候迎身而上，尤其是那些你非常熟悉的东西；你觉得自己处在有利位置去利用它……

turns.en: You feel like you are positioned to take advantage of it, maybe make it go away. Every crisis teaches and reinforces that you want to stress test. You want to think carefully about what factors could cause a drawdown in your portfolio. You want to think hard about what's the difference between a drawdown and a capital impairment because those are different things.
turns.zh: ……甚至让它消失。每一次危机都在教育并强化同一个道理：你要做压力测试，要仔细思考哪些因素可能让组合出现回撤，要认真想清楚回撤和资本受损的区别——因为这是两回事。

turns.en: Also, thinking about what doesn't work. What are you relying on in terms of institutions, courts, banks, counterparties, these kinds of things. You learn them in your first crisis and you never forget them. Stuff begins to rhyme for you. The most important thing that we learn is good people who are curious and have thought through things and can maintain their curiosity, bearings, and have a real sense of rigor and purpose are vital to those moments. We are in a
turns.zh: 还要思考哪些环节会失灵：你在机构、法院、银行、交易对手这些方面依赖的到底是什么。你在第一次危机里学会，就永远不会忘记。一切开始像押韵一样重演。我们学到的最重要的东西是：好的、有好奇心、把问题想透、能保持好奇与定力、真正有严谨精神和目标感的人，对那些时刻至关重要。我们正处在一个……

turns.en: moment where a lot of stuff does rhyme with other periods. A lot of people talk about having deja vu to the dot com era. That's also true locally in the space that we are applying our craft, which is you've seen a lot of risk capital go somewhere else. We're seeing enormously mispriced things and some pretty ordinary stuff on what looks like a sunny day economically with volatility low, the VIX low, a lot of liquidity to trade things. You would expect
turns.zh: ……很多事情确实和其他时期押韵的时刻。很多人说有一种回到 dot-com 时代的既视感。在我们施展手艺的这个局部领域里同样如此：你看到大量风险资本去了别处。我们看到巨大的错误定价，而在经济看起来风和日丽的日子里——波动率低、VIX 低、流动性充裕、什么都能交易——却出现一些相当平庸的东西。你本来会期待……

turns.en: there would be more price discrimination, more people trying to trade the right asset. We see a little bit less of that. That is also similar to dot com. You do learn to think about patterns. Liquidity is good not just because you have cash. If you have fairly liquid positions, you can move things around. You're not going to predict where it is that people are going to decide to throw the babies out with the bathwater. On the middle of COVID, we're buying treasuries
turns.zh: ……会有更多的价格甄别，更多的人努力交易正确的资产，但我们看到的反而少一些。这一点也和 dot-com 时期相似。你确实要学会思考模式。流动性好不只是因为你手里有现金。如果你有相当流动的头寸，你就能腾挪。你不可能预测到人们会在哪里决定把孩子连同洗澡水一起泼出去。新冠疫情最剧烈的时候，我们在买……

turns.en: in escrow at 80 cents on the dollar. Things happen. You want to be able to move your portfolio around so you can take advantage of those things. How have you gone about identifying talent for your team? The Yale model and David's magic was people, people, people. I'm told when they cleaned out his office and they pulled open his drawer, there was a no card that said people, people, people. That at the heart of all of this stuff. When I first met Gabe Sunshine,
turns.zh: ……存管（escrow）账户里的国债，按 1 美元 80 美分。事情总会发生。你要能让组合动起来，才能利用这些事情。你们是怎么为团队物色人才的？耶鲁模式和 David 的魔力就是：人、人、人。我听说他们清理他办公室时拉开抽屉，里面有一张便笺，写着“人、人、人”。这就是所有这一切的核心。我第一次见到 Gabe Sunshine 的时候……

turns.zh: ……他来高盛面试，对金融一无所知。他是最有才华的人。所谓才华，不只是有极高的智商，而是勤奋、好奇心、关于我们知道什么和不知道什么的谦逊，这一整套环绕在周围的东西——这来自这种以人为先的思考方式。这是我做的这件事里很有乐趣的一部分。

turns.en: It gets you out in the world and you meet people. turns.zh: 它把你带到外面的世界去见人。你在多元的背景、多元的教育路径中找到可以聊的有趣的人，找到所有那些被市场点亮的人，他们喜欢我们想做的事情的那种连贯与清晰。我们不做任何宏观预测。我们找 alpha，利用 alpha，让价格收敛。

turns.en: What are some of the characteristics that make someone successful as an investor in this style? The first thing that transcends everything else is curiosity and a desire to know. There's other things that have to come with it, math, rigor, a taste for reading things, a lot of humility about whether you do in fact know. Some desire to self-test yourself, to be able to explain it, to be able to challenge your own ideas, to be able to challenge others' ideas and still have them
turns.zh: 在这种风格里成为成功的投资人，有哪些特质？凌驾于其他一切之上的第一样，是好奇心和求知的欲望。但其他东西必须跟上来：数学、严谨、喜欢阅读、对“你是不是真的知道”保持大量谦逊，有一种自我检验的愿望，能够把事情解释清楚，能够挑战自己的想法，也能挑战别人的想法，而第二天对方还愿意……

turns.en: talk to you the next day. Those things are the characteristics that make people successful at this. One of the things that makes people successful at something is they like it.

turns.en: Markets are interesting and puzzles are interesting. For the kind of person who's really curious, you like puzzles and you're given a puzzle and you're more curious about it because you have not yet solved it and you're still waiting for that. That's your person.
turns.zh: 市场有意思，谜题有意思。对真正好奇的那类人来说，你喜欢谜题，有人给你一个谜题，你反而更好奇，因为你还没解开它，你还在等那个时刻。这样的人才是对的人。

When I think about alignment, what matters are is investors. We want to make sure that every single person who's committing capital is aligned with the investor. First easy way, make them investors. We want senior people to get paid

turns.en: more when investors do well. As you've grown over the years, had a bunch of the same partners and brought more people in, how have you thought about matching the appropriate size of the activity with the
turns.zh: ……在投资人赚得好时拿到更多。我们会去想，怎么让大家去投资自己的同事，去协作，去产出我们所说的公共品——模型、方法、别人能用的东西。你要激励人们去做你希望他们做的事。这些年你们不断成长，一直是那批合伙人，又引进了更多人，你们怎么思考让业务规模与……

turns.en: opportunity set? The opportunity set has to be in charge. We don't stock the lake, we just fish here. There are moments in the world where rates are inefficient and you're having food fight every day for capital. There's moments where central banks are managing every single yield curve.
turns.zh: ……机会集相匹配？必须让机会集当家。我们不往湖里放鱼苗，我们只在这里钓鱼。世界有些时候利率很无效率，你每天都在为资本抢成一锅粥；有些时候央行在管理每一条收益率曲线。

turns.en: There's nothing to do because the non-economic agent has a spline and buys the cheap bonds in the name of QE. Those worlds are different. It's a fun moment to be in the second one.

turns.en: One of the best things that happened from this partnership with David is this dialogue about the opportunity set. Trying to carefully describe what do we think the opportunity set is? What can we deliver given the opportunities in the market? Having capital that is sized for the opportunity set we have, which doesn't have much to do with us. We have to be respectful of that. It's a natural outgrowth of the rest of what we do. It was hammered home to us early in our career that it
turns.zh: 和 David 这段伙伴关系里最好的事情之一，就是这场关于机会集的对话。努力仔细描述：我们认为机会集是什么？在市场给出的机会之下我们能交付什么？让资本的规模匹配我们拥有的机会集——而机会集和我们没多大关系，我们必须尊重这一点。这是我们其他工作方式的自然延伸。职业生涯早期，他们就把这个道理深深砸进我们脑子里：它是……

turns.en: was part of it. turns.en: A lot of bonds. The last two decades or more, there has always been somebody who wanted to buy bonds. First, it was Japanese, then the Chinese with the conundrum. turns.zh: 很多债券。过去二十年或更久，总有人想买债券。先是日本人，然后是中国人，带着那个“未解之谜”（conundrum）。那很复杂，但他们确实想买我们的债券。从 2008 年到 QE 结束，我们自己的财政部——那帮人在买债券。那现在，买家是谁？财政部还想再多买一点债券。

turns.en: They want to move the duration in. They're going to do some buybacks. That's also interesting. We get to this new era of policy experimentation. turns.zh: 他们想把久期拉进来。他们要做一些回购。这也很有意思。我们进入了一个政策实验的新时代。前三年有 43 个工具在描述同一个利率过程，其中一些带 call，一些带 put，不可能所有东西每天都定价正确。这对我们做的生意是好事。

turns.en: What's an example of something you've looked at in the explosion of lending to the tech ecosystem with all the build out of what's happening in AI?

turns.en: Some of them think they need to survive. Maybe on Monday they thought they were going to win the whole thing, and on Wednesday they didn't want to survive. It's fluid. turns.zh: 有些则觉得自己需要活下来就好。也许周一他们还觉得会赢得一切，周三就发现能活下来都不容易。局面是流动的。不管是什么，我觉得他们并不特别担心基点。也许 10 年能有 32% 的投资回报。他们想借的，是尽可能多、尽可能长期的钱，什么币种能借就借什么。有时候他们是一个数据中心的租户……

turns.en: center and they sign a lease. Sometimes they're just issuing an IG bond. It makes perfect sense that they're not that fussed up about the basis point stuff. turns.zh: ……签一份租约；有时候他们就发一笔 IG 债券。他们不那么纠结基点的事，完全说得通。随着利率从 4.25% 走到现在的 4.61%，这确实会冲击那些传统的抠基点的人，比如一家杠杆加了无数倍的保险公司。这是一个生态系统。超大规模云厂商这件事，放在单一主体内部看有意思，跨币种看也有意思。Google 一出场，第一笔……

turns.en: Over the last couple of years, there's been a lot of activity, liability management exercises, that have more to do with the people in the bonds, how they're playing those games when things run into trouble. I'm curious, how do you think about where mathematical relationships can go awry because of the motivations of the people playing the game and the game theory alongside it?
turns.zh: 过去几年，债务管理操作（liability management exercises）很活跃，那更多地关乎债券里的持有人本身——当事情陷入困境时他们怎么玩这些游戏。我很好奇：当玩家的动机、以及伴随其间的博弈论介入时，数学关系会在哪里出问题，你们是怎么思考的？

turns.en: This will be a whole podcast of its own. When I think about the evolution of our corporate team becoming involved in this stuff, there is a change. There's a lot about what people are doing, who's zooming who. There's an expression in that market. If you're not at the table, you're on the menu, which not that appealing but might be true. These things don't start out as soap operas. They start out as situations with big capital stacks and legal contracts.
turns.zh: 这足够单独做一整期播客了。回看我们做公司债的团队介入这些事情的演变，确实有变化。里面有很多是人们在做什么、谁在碾压谁。那个市场里有句话：如果你不在桌边，你就在菜单上——不太中听，但可能是真的。这些事一开始并不是肥皂剧，一开始是带着庞大资本结构和法律合约的局面。

turns.en: The math is the least of it. What's enforceable? Who else has voting rights? I don't know that it turns out to be personalities as much as it turns out to be constraints. What's important for this business going forward to be either an ongoing concern or to restructure entirely? Rates are where they are. People borrowed a lot of money in 21, 22. They are going to need to refinance it.
turns.zh: 数学反而是最次要的。什么是可执行的？还有谁有投票权？我觉得最终起作用的与其说是个性，不如说是约束。这家公司往前走，重要的是作为持续经营主体，还是彻底重组？利率就是现在这个样子。人们在 21、22 年借了很多钱，将来需要再融资。

turns.en: There's different rates now. If they don't have a business model that allows them to roll that stuff you'll have to see stuff. It's this qualitative understanding of what is possible or likely.
turns.zh: 现在是不同的利率了。如果他们没有能滚动这些债务的商业模式，你就会开始看到一些事情。这是一种定性理解：什么是可能的，什么是或然的……

turns.en: It's the quantitative understanding of what cash flows are owed, what rights accrue to whom, if those cash flows aren't paid. Where's the security interest and how do you get at it?
turns.zh: ……也是一种定量理解：欠着哪些现金流，如果这些现金流不付，哪些权利会落到谁头上。担保权益在哪里，你怎么去够到它？

turns.en: What kind of group is involved? That stuff's fascinating. I don't think anybody would expect it to be completely efficient. To roll up your sleeves and get involved in this, you ought to get paid a reasonable amount on risk capital. It's been a few years you've been doing this.
turns.zh: 涉及什么样的团体？这些东西太迷人了。没人会觉得它是完全有效的。你要卷起袖子参与这种事，就应该在风险资本上拿到合理的回报。你们做这个也有几年了。

turns.en: Would love to hear your thoughts on what the next period of time at Bracebridge looks like. The next three or five years look a lot like the last three to five years with the excitement of what's going on in financial markets, which is truly extraordinary, plus AI, a lot of compute, exciting team of partners who are hitting on all cylinders. We have the best team we've ever had.
turns.zh: 很想听听你对 Bracebridge 下一阶段的看法。未来三五年和过去三五年很像：金融市场正在发生的一切让人兴奋，真的非常不寻常，再加上 AI、大量算力，一支所有引擎全开的、让人兴奋的合伙人团队。我们有史以来最好的团队。

turns.en: We have an extraordinary opportunity set. We have a really important moment to play a role in people's portfolios by providing them with diversification. How about for you? I'm excited to be part of that team, learn from our mistakes, stand on our shoulders, try not to make the same mistake twice. Imagine if you don't even have to make my mistakes. If we could pass some of that on, this is just a great moment in markets. Happy to be part of it.
turns.zh: 我们有一个非凡的机会集。这是一个真正重要的时刻，我们可以通过提供分散化，在人们的组合里发挥作用。对你个人呢？我很兴奋能成为这支团队的一部分，从我们的错误中学习，站在彼此的肩膀上，尽量不重犯同一个错误。想象一下，如果你连我犯过的错误都不必经历。如果我们能把其中一些传递下去——现在就是市场里一个美好的时刻，很高兴参与其中。

turns.en: I'd love to ask you about some of the other activities you've been involved with alongside of Bracebridge. The first I'd be remiss if I didn't ask you about Brown's investment committee, what you learned from that experience. It's been an enormous pleasure and privilege to watch Joe, Dowling, and then Jane build their portfolio and their program, train junior people, they use AI.
turns.zh: 我很想问问你在 Bracebridge 之外参与的其他一些事情。首先，如果不问你布朗大学投资委员会的经历、你从中学到了什么，我就太失职了。能看着 Joe、Dowling，然后是 Jane 打造他们的组合和项目、培养年轻人、用 AI……

turns.en: Brown is a great group of stewards focused on asset liability management, how Brown's going to have resources to fulfill its educational mission. That's been great. I remember that one of the first investment committees that I was at, there was somebody who brings up a native conversation about this correlation between stocks and bonds. It's a moment that's different than this moment.
turns.zh: ……是莫大的愉快和荣幸。布朗有一群很棒的受托人，专注于资产负债管理，专注于布朗将如何拥有资源去完成它的教育使命。这很好。我记得我参加的最早几次投委会中，有一次，有人提起一段关于股票和债券相关性的对话，那是与今天不同的一个时刻。

turns.en: I don't remember who's running the endowment at the time. They're like, we had these bonds and they earned this. They're like, we need more returns than that. You can need whatever you want.
turns.zh: 我不记得当时是谁在管捐赠基金了。他们说，我们持有这些债券，它们赚了这些收益。他们说，我们需要比这更高的回报。你想“需要”什么就可以“需要”什么。

turns.en: That's what bonds yield. Bonds change. Now we think about people have many fewer bonds in their portfolios because they're not reliably anti-correlated. We are in a different world where there's a huge demand to borrow money. If we see a slight downturn in the economy, I don't think anybody is completely convinced that they're going to act in a way that's going to be ballast for their portfolio. Well, it's interesting for me to see people unpack that, think about how is this
turns.zh: 债券就是那个收益水平。债券会变。现在我们会想，人们的组合里债券少多了，因为它们不再可靠地负相关。我们处在一个不同的世界，这里有巨大的借钱需求。如果经济出现轻微下行，我不觉得有谁完全确信它们还会以充当组合压舱石的方式行动。对我来说，看人们拆解这件事、思考这个捐赠基金到底要怎么运转……

turns.en: endowment going to work? It's given me real insight into how people are smart and doing incredibly interesting things on the regular. They're not as intimately involved in the minutia of pricing an asset, portfolio construction, or investing. My involvement in Brown, what made me come to the table in 2012. First of all, leadership. Chris Paxton is an extraordinary leader. It is always a pleasure to watch someone lead you learn every single minute of it.
turns.zh: ……很有意思。这让我真正看到平时他们是多么聪明，做着多么不可思议的事情。他们不像我们这样深切参与给资产定价、组合构建或投资的细枝末节。我参与布朗、2012 年上桌的原因，首先是领导力。Christina Paxson 是一位非凡的领导者。看着有人领导永远是一种享受，其中的每一分钟你都在学习。

turns.en: The brain science stuff that I got to do, they were talented people and they were about to do something extraordinary. They're trying to figure out, how do I pick between this and that? How do I pick between doing the gut brain axis, coming up with a process to figure out what areas we're going to invest in? I felt like I could learn a lot about brain sensors. It was super exciting and also bring discipline to that activity. That's been fun and they also are committed
turns.zh: 我参与的那些脑科学事务，是一群有才华的人，正要做非凡的事。他们在琢磨：这个和那个之间怎么选？做不做肠脑轴（gut-brain axis）？怎么建立一个流程来决定我们要投入哪些方向？我觉得我能学到很多脑科学的东西，特别兴奋，同时也能给这件事带来纪律。这很有趣，他们也致力于……

turns.en: to training young people. When you train for a postdoc, there's a lot of skill wrap around just like what we do. People need a lot of skills to do arbitrage. People need to be able to communicate with their colleagues. They need to be able to explain to somebody why they're wrong and have the conversation keep going on. They need to be able to notice things about what they're doing that need course correcting and go get help. They need to be able to use new tools. They need to be able
turns.zh: ……培养年轻人。带一个博士后（postdoc）的时候，周围裹着一大堆技能，就像我们做的一样。人们做套利需要很多技能：要能和同事沟通，要向某人解释他为什么错了、并且让对话继续下去，要能注意到自己做的事需要纠偏并且去求助，要能用新工具，要能意识到……

turns.en: to know they need new tools and they don't have them yet. There's a lot of things that are similar. It's fun to get out of your own space where you're building out something to meet a narrow and specific purpose to bring that to a place where somebody's trying to decide, should we do this or that? How many people can we have in the graduate program and still serve them correctly?
turns.zh: ……自己需要新工具而还没有。很多事情是相通的。从你自己的领域里走出去是有趣的——你在那里为一个狭窄而具体的目的打磨东西，然后把它带到一个有人要做决定的地方：我们该做这个还是那个？研究生项目收多少人，我们才能既收得下又善待他们？

turns.en: Diane Litzkin, who's an extraordinary leader, seeing Chris Paxson in action, that's been fabulous for me as a leader myself. It's made my world a lot bigger. You see what pressures people are under to see how people make choices. When we're making good choices, when the choices we're making is because of what everyone else is doing or what we said we would do before, before things change, when all of a sudden we're in this world where we're making choices about
turns.zh: Diane Litzkin 也是一位非凡的领导者，看着 Christina Paxson 的实际作为，对我自己做领导者太有帮助了。它让我的世界大了很多。你会看到人们承受着什么压力，看到人们如何做选择。什么时候我们在做出好的选择，什么时候我们的选择只是因为别人都在这么做，或者因为我们在事情变化之前说过要这么做——当突然之间，我们身处这样一个世界：我们做的选择关乎……

turns.en: securities that are not about the price of those things or the risk of just a return, they're about us. What are some of the views that you have now in that forum that are different from other people's? That it might be good to just sit and listen.
turns.zh: ……证券——而这些选择无关它们的价格，也不只是回报的风险——而是关乎我们自己。你在那个场合里有什么和别人不同的观点？大概就是：坐下来好好听，可能是件好事。

turns.en: People are not forward-looking. People like to suck. For a lot of people, that's their way of understanding something. I want to make sure I get a chance to ask you a couple closing questions. What is the most rewarding thing you do outside of work?
turns.zh: 人们不向前看。很多人就是喜欢唱反调。对很多人来说，那就是他们理解事物的方式。我想确保有机会问你几个收尾的问题。你在工作中之外最有成就感的事情是什么？

turns.en: We're taking out parenting, most rewarding and challenging thing any of us do, most purposeful thing. My kids are big. I think I've managed to work myself out of a job.
turns.zh: 我们把养育除外——那是我们每个人做的最有回报、也最具挑战、最有目标感的事。我的孩子都大了。我想我已经成功地把自己从这份工作里“优化”掉了。

turns.en: Forward-looking. I'm still involved with brain science at Brown. I'm still in the corporation at Brown. It's been quite rewarding. What was your first paid job and what did you learn from it?
turns.zh: 要向前看嘛。我仍然参与布朗的脑科学事务，仍然在布朗的 Corporation（校董会）里任职。这些都很有回报。你的第一份有报酬的工作是什么？你从中学到了什么？

turns.en: I was a lifeguard at a JCC. I got a gig as a swim teacher out of it. That was sweet. If you meet an older person who decides they want to learn how to swim, if they just relax, they can learn to swim. Which two people have had the biggest impact on your professional life?
turns.zh: 我在 JCC（犹太社区中心）当过救生员，还从中得到一份游泳教练的活儿，很美好。如果你遇到一位上了年纪的人决定要学游泳，只要他们放松，就能学会游泳。哪两个人对你的职业生涯影响最大？

turns.en: I wonder if another person asked me what answer the same way is one of these funny, cognitive psych tests. Davis Wentzen, who we all knew and loved, and Gabe Sunshine, my partner who I started the business with who's been an unbelievable thought partner, rigor-demander, careful investor, side-by-side with me for however many years we've been doing this.
turns.zh: 我在想，如果换一个人用同样的方式问我，我的回答会不会不一样——这有点像那种有趣的认知心理学测试。David Swenson，我们都认识并爱戴他；还有 Gabe Sunshine，我的合伙人，和我一起创业的人——一个不可思议的思考伙伴、对严谨的苛求者、审慎的投资人，和我肩并肩做了我们共事的这么多年。

turns.en: Most may not know you're married to well-known economist Andre Schleifer. You've both had incredible runs on independent career paths. I don't think I've ever asked you how you first met and what it's been like. Around the time that there's this crash, I met this young economist who was an assistant professor at the University of Chicago who had written his dissertation about market efficiency and used index inclusion for stocks
turns.zh: 很多人可能不知道，你的丈夫是著名经济学家 Andrei Shleifer。你们俩各自走出了一段不可思议的独立职业道路。我好像从来没问过你们最初是怎么认识的、这一切是什么感受。大概就在那次股灾前后，我遇见了一位年轻的经济学家，他是芝加哥大学的助理教授，博士论文写的市场有效性，用股票被纳入指数……

turns.en: as a way to show that markets aren't efficient because nothing's happened to the company. I was fascinated by this person. First of all, he's an enormously supportive person.
turns.zh: ……作为证明市场无效的方法——因为公司本身什么都没发生。我被这个人迷住了。首先，他是一个无比支持我的人。

turns.en: Second of all, it's great to have somebody in your life who is a real life of the mind. It also reminds you when you're doing things at Brown how important the university is, how important undergrads are at a university. The difference that education makes in all of our lives, the specific things from sitting in the probability class to the soft things of having a roommate that you have to get along with, who comes from a different part of the world.
turns.zh: 其次，你的生活里有一个真正在过思想生活的人，这太好了。这也会提醒你在布朗做事时，大学有多么重要，本科生在大学里有多么重要。教育在我们所有人一生里造成的差异——具体的，比如坐在概率课里；柔性的，比如你必须和一个来自世界另一个角落的室友好好相处。

turns.en: Professors that you maybe cross paths with or maybe you cross swords with, this power of the university having had the privilege to be included in that community, to be with somebody who had a life of the mind who's trying to get to the bottom of things all the time, write books, move the frontier has been enormously fabulous for me and I'm enormously grateful that this just happened.
turns.zh: 那些你或许擦肩而过、或许交锋过的教授。大学的力量，有幸被接纳进那个共同体，和一个过思想生活的人在一起——他永远在试图把事情追到根上、写书、推进前沿——这对我来说太好了，我深深感激这一切发生了。

turns.en: What advice would you give someone who is interested in getting involved in this business? This is an extraordinary moment to be a young person in markets. You can come and add value right away. You're going to get up the curve faster. You're going to learn things. You're going to at least have context when you ask your questions. Markets are the most interesting thing.
turns.zh: 对于一个有意进入这一行的人，你会给什么建议？对一个年轻人来说，这是在市场里一个非凡的时刻。你一进来就能创造价值，你会更快地沿着曲线爬升，你会学到东西，至少你提问的时候有了语境。市场是最有意思的东西。

turns.en: This is a really exciting moment to be a young person in market and I think there's going to be a lot of opportunity. All right, Nance, one more. What life lesson have you learned that you wish you knew a lot earlier in life? I wasn't as indexed as I am now on how much process matters.
turns.zh: 对一个年轻人来说，这是市场里真正令人兴奋的时刻，我想未来会有大量机会。好，Nancy，最后一个。你学到了什么人生教训，希望你更早懂得？我以前不像现在这样，懂得流程有多重要。

turns.en: I've known since I was a kid that people mattered. You could count on people, they were reliable, they were rigorous, curious, they wanted to know what the right answer was, but I didn't know at the beginning how much process mattered. Process plus people is how you get performance. I wish I knew that when I was 18. Nancy, thanks so much for taking the time to do this. Thanks for having me, Ted. Thanks for listening all the way to the end.
turns.zh: 我从小就知道人很重要：人可以指望，他们可靠、严谨、好奇，想知道正确答案是什么。但一开始我不知道流程有多重要。流程加上人，才是业绩的来源。我希望我 18 岁就知道这一点。Nancy，非常感谢你抽出时间做这期节目。谢谢你邀请我，Ted。谢谢听到最后的每一位。

turns.en: If you made it this far, how about one ask for me? Tell one friend about the show. It's the best way to keep growing this incredible community.
turns.zh: 如果你听到了这里，能否帮我一个忙？把节目告诉一位朋友。这是让这个了不起的社群继续成长的最佳方式。

turns.en: Thanks so much and until the next one, stay curious and keep compounding knowledge, relationships, and capital a little bit at a time.
